text.p: Oil and wheat prices ended firmer among commodities of Australian interest, while base metals prices were mixed and gold eased slightly. The CRB index rose 0.24 to 243.33.
Base metals on the LME mixed, with most markets able to rally off their lows without showing any sign of sustaining a definite trend, traders said.
Price movements were largely influenced by technical considerations, with trade interest at a low ebb, they said.

Copper whipped around between just below $2,300 and just above $2,260, remaining well within its well-worn range. There was also little significant movement on the spreads, with the cash/threes backwardation remaining around $19. Last three months business was at $2,290 a tonne, up $12 from Tuesday.

Aluminium climbed off its $1,687 lows, but still ended easier and under $1,700. Last business was at $1,696, down $19. Some said that the 4,100-tonne stock increase -- the second successive daily rise -- may herald a change in the inventory trend. But others said it was premature to suggest stock falls had now ended.

Zinc managed to stage a recovery from depressed midsession levels, pulled up by the trend in copper and aluminium. However, the upturn still left prices adrift of $1,500 overhead, closing $5 firmer at $1,485.
Nickel prices fell away during the afternoon, as sell-stops were hit when chart support levels were breached. Last business was at $6,510, down $190 from Tuesday.
Lead was steady throughout the session, and finished at $607, up $10. Tin moved off its lows, and closed at $5,410, down just $5. Alloy was at a little-changed $1,505/10.

GOLD - COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed after a choppy trading session, in which gold and silver tracked the volatile action in U.S. bonds and stocks and the U.S. dollar. COMEX December gold ended down 10 cents at $330.70 an ounce, after seeing a session high at $333.20, not far from the top of the month old range around $335.00. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted around $326.90/40 an ounce.

GRAINS - CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed firmer on a rally in nearby soybean contracts, traders said. CBOT SRW wheat futures closed 1/4 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 1/4 at $3.61-1/4. December was up 1-1/4 at $3.77-3/4.

OIL - U.S. crude prices attracted mostly firmer prices Wednesday, but lagged gains in gasoline. September crude finished 20 cents a barrel higher at $20.19 while September heating oil settled 0.94 cent higher at 56.04 cents a gallon.

SUGAR - CSCE world sugar futures closed barely lower after setting the range early in the day and then drifting amid light volume. The spot October contract settled 0.02 cent weaker at 11.49 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.58 to 11.41 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.02 cent lower to 0.04 cent firmer.
